title: 몇 시까지? 어디까지? 끝을 말하는 「까지」
objective: By the end, you can use 까지 to say when something ends or how far you go, and use it with 부터 (start time) and 에서 (start place).
summary: Learn to use 까지 to show where a time or a trip ends, usually together with 부터 or 에서.

task.title: USE 부터, 에서, AND 까지
task.line: Read each item, then fill in, choose, or write the Korean as the instruction asks.

forms.when: After a time word. It has the same form after any noun, with or without a final consonant.
To give both the start time and the end time.
forms.exampleMeaning: I work from Monday to Friday.

forms.when: To give the start place and the end place of a trip.
forms.exampleMeaning: I go from home to work by bus.

forms.when: With a request or a plan that must be done by a time (no later than that time).

watchOut: 5시에까지 와요 (X) → 5시까지 와요 (O): After a time word, do not put 에 before 까지. Use 까지 alone.
9시에서 6시까지 일해요 (OK, spoken) → 9시부터 6시까지 일해요 (more standard): For a start time, use 부터. For a start place, use 에서.
6시까지 일해요 = work until 6 (all the time up to 6). 6시까지 오세요 = come by 6 (not later). Look at the verb to find the meaning.
exercises: Fill in the blanks with 부터 or 까지: 방학은 7월____ 8월____예요.
Fill in the blanks with 에서 or 까지: 서울____ 부산____ 기차로 가요.
Choose the correct sentence: ①3시에까지 기다려요. ②3시까지 기다려요.
Complete the sentence with 까지: You get in a taxi and want to go to the airport (공항). What do you say? ____ 가 주세요.
Does 까지 mean 'by' or 'until' here? ①수요일까지 책을 주세요. ②수요일까지 여행해요.
Answer in a full Korean sentence. Lunch is 12:00–1:00: 몇 시부터 몇 시까지 점심시간이에요?
answers: ① by (give it to me by Wednesday, not later) ② until (travel until Wednesday)
